reason: The description captures the high-level purpose correctly — extracting a ZIP entry by index into a caller-supplied buffer without allocation — and correctly notes the no-alloc intent, buffer size requirement, and error-on-failure behavior. However, it significantly mischaracterizes the 'no_alloc' guarantee: the implementation *will* fall back to allocating a temporary read buffer internally when neither an in-memory archive nor a user read buffer is available, so the 'no allocation' claim is not strictly true. The description also omits several important behavioral details: the `flags` parameter (including `MZ_ZIP_FLAG_COMPRESSED_DATA` for raw compressed output), the optional `st` file-stat pointer that bypasses the internal stat lookup, CRC32 verification after decompression, support for both stored and deflate methods, encryption/patch-file rejection, directory and zero-length file early-return as success, local header parsing and validation, and the three distinct read-buffer strategies (in-memory archive, user buffer, or fallback allocation). The return type is `mz_bool`, not an enum. These omissions would make it difficult to implement the function correctly from the description alone.
missing_functionality: flags parameter and MZ_ZIP_FLAG_COMPRESSED_DATA behavior (raw compressed data output path)
optional st (mz_zip_archive_file_stat*) parameter that skips internal file_stat lookup
CRC32 verification of decompressed (or stored) data
three read-buffer strategies: in-memory archive pointer, user-supplied buffer, and fallback internal allocation
encryption and patch-file detection returning unsupported error
method validation: only stored (0) and deflate supported
directory entries and zero-length files return MZ_TRUE immediately
local directory header parsing and signature validation
return type is mz_bool, not an enum
incorrect_or_misleading_points: Description states the function relies on caller-supplied buffers 'rather than allocating memory itself' — the implementation does allocate a temporary read buffer when no user read buffer and no in-memory archive is present
Description says the return value is an 'enum' status — it is actually mz_bool (MZ_TRUE/MZ_FALSE)
